title: Attention sparsity triggered path thrashing — post-incident action playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: During a capacity event on 2026-02-20 we observed recurring throughput and tail-latency spikes for a subset of long-context chat workloads. This ticket contains the follow-up investigation, hypotheses, and concrete remediation tasks to prevent 'path thrashing' in the kernel selection/scheduler that appears correlated with attention sparsity patterns and intermittent KV-cache warmup failures.

Why this is unique: unlike prior kernel-mismatch regressions, this incident only appears for inputs with extreme attention sparsity (long prefix, many padding tokens, or repeated early BOS tokens) which caused the scheduling heuristic to oscillate between a sparse-attention optimized kernel and the default dense path. That oscillation amplified queueing/backpressure and triggered autoscaler overshoot on dedicated pools.

Goals: 1) Stabilize kernel selection heuristics for sparse-attention shaped workloads. 2) Mitigate immediate customer impact via safe fallback and autoscaler tuning. 3) Deploy long-term guardrails and monitoring to detect path thrash earlier.
timeline: 2026-02-20: Incident detected by SLO alert (p95 latency crossing 2.5x baseline) during evening traffic spike.
2026-02-20: On-call traced pattern to a subset of job traces with >70% attention sparsity; reproduced locally on a dev rig with synthetic traces.
2026-02-21: Initial mitigation: pinned affected capacity to dense kernel (manual route override) to stop oscillation — latency returned to baseline.
2026-02-22: Eng investigation discovered interactions between kernel-probing logic and batch-eviction window; heuristics rewrote route decisions at the batch boundary under memory pressure.
2026-02-23: Postmortem draft and this follow-up ticket created with prioritized actions.
2026-03-03: Canary for probe-suppression patch rolled out to 10% of traffic for runtime-1.22; observed elimination of oscillation in canary traces.
2026-03-12: Ops completed autoscaler smoothing parameter update to reduce overshoot in dedicated pools.
2026-03-13: This ticket: In progress — remaining items scheduled for runtime-1.22.1 and runtime-1.23
root_cause_summary: A combination of attention-sparsity-driven kernel preference toggles and an aggressive kernel-probing window caused the scheduler to flip execution paths at batch boundaries. Under high concurrency this produced transient KV-cache warmup failures and increased per-request queuing. The autoscaler reacted to short-term throughput changes and added capacity that briefly increased scheduling entropy, creating a feedback loop that prolonged tail latency.
mitigations: Short-term: pin affected traffic to dense kernel via per-route override and disable aggressive probe windows (rollback knob) — done for incident window.
Medium-term: implement probe suppression when attention sparsity > threshold and when KV-cache hit-rate < X% for two consecutive requests.
Long-term: introduce hysteresis to kernel selection (min dwell time before switching) and expose guidance knobs in Dedicated autoscaler to prevent rapid capacity oscillation.
Observability: add a dedicated 'path-thrash' metric counting kernel-switch events per-request and alert when >10% of requests in 1m show >1 switch.
Customer communications: notify top-affected customers with remediation summary and recommend model/prompt fixes (avoid pathological padding sequences) where feasible.
tasks: T1: Merge probe-suppression patch (PR #4821) into runtime-1.22 branch and backport to runtime-1.21 LTS. Owner: Liam O'Connor. Due: 2026-03-16.
T2: Add kernel-switch hysteresis (min_switch_ms) and unit tests. Owner: Priya Singh. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-20.
T3: Add 'path-thrash' telemetry + dashboard and pager rule. Owner: Observability team (Evan Ruiz). Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-18.
T4: Autoscaler smoothing parameter tuning for Dedicated pools and add canary rollback automation. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Estimate: 2. Done: 2026-03-12.
T5: Run regression suite with synthetic high-sparsity traces and publish results to runtime-stability doc. Owner: QA (Rachel Kim). Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-19.
T6: Customer outreach draft and templates for CS/Success. Owner: Solutions (Noah Bryant). Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-03-17.
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 — probe-suppression: reduce kernel probing for high-sparsity traces (canaryed)
https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4899 — add min_switch_ms hysteresis and unit tests
https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3104 — autoscaler smoothing and canary rollback hooks
notes: Design trade-off: hysteresis prevents rapid recovery when a true workload shift occurs. We'll tune min_switch_ms conservatively and expose per-customer override for Dedicated.
We considered changing model-selection to prefer stable kernels (avoid switching) but that would increase cost for some steady-state sparse workloads; chose hysteresis + probe-suppression instead.
QA regression harness: synthetic generator added new sparse attention scenario (prefix-length heavy) to prevent regressions in future releases.
